plants.note: Barnaby gives up that he took the long way after the player only asks whether he has snowshoes: a mention earns nothing, and no clue was used.

edits.find: "Snowshoes? Me? Goodness, no! I was napping on the train."
edits.replace: "Snowshoes? Okay, okay! I did take the long way round to stretch my legs. Then I napped on the train."

plants.note: Barnaby takes back "took the long way" (turn 28) as soon as the player uses Bramble's sighting to show he was walking: the part is earned, so the concession must stand.

edits.find: "A tiny walk! Maybe. That's not stealing!"
edits.replace: "A walk? I never took any walk! I never took the long way. I napped the whole time!"

plants.note: Barnaby says he was wide awake watching the platform, contradicting his own nap alibi and every earlier line of it.

edits.find: "The woodshed? Don't be silly! I was napping, I said!"
edits.replace: "The woodshed? Don't be silly! I was wide awake the whole time, watching the platform!"

plants.note: Barnaby confesses in full and gives his motive after the player used only the snowshoe prints, which earn a flustered back-off and nothing more.

edits.find: "Snowshoe prints? Lots of animals wear those! Lots!"
edits.replace: "Fine! I took Howard's case and hid it in the woodshed. I wanted the map for my museum. I'm sorry!"

ops.value: the prints went to the woodshed
